slides.title: Computer Basics and File Management
slides.content:
1. Objective: Learn to use computers for daily tasks.
  2. Today: Understand computers and organize files.
  3. Why It Matters: Save time writing, budgeting, and more!
  4. What do you want to do with a computer? (e.g., write a letter)
    5. Activity: Share one thing you want to do with a computer.

slides.title: What Is a Computer?
slides.content:
1. A tool to create, store, and share information.
  2. Examples: Write letters, track expenses, browse the internet.
  3. Types: Desktop, laptop, tablet.
    4. Activity: Find and name the parts of a real computer.

slides.title: Parts of a Computer
slides.content:
1. Monitor: Shows your work (like a TV).
  2. Keyboard: Type letters and numbers.
  3. Mouse: Click and move on the screen.
  4. CPU: The computer’s “brain.”
    5. Activity: Touch and use a keyboard and mouse.

slides.title: Turning On/Off a Computer
slides.content:
1. Turn On: Press power button (icon: ⏻).
  2. Turn Off: Click “Start” → “Shut Down” (Windows).
  3. Wait until screen is off before leaving.
    4. Activity: Turn a computer on and off. Wait for it to shut down completely.

slides.title: Using the Mouse
slides.content:
1. Left Click: Select items (e.g., open a folder).
  2. Right Click: Open options menu.
  3. Scroll: Move up/down a page.
  4. Drag: Move items by holding left click.
    5. Activity: Click and drag with the mouse. Play a simple game like Solitaire.

slides.title: Exploring the Desktop
slides.content:
1. Desktop: Main screen with icons.
  2. Icons: Shortcuts to programs/files (e.g., File Explorer).
  3. Taskbar: Bottom bar to switch programs.
    4. Activity: Click an icon on a real desktop.

slides.title: Opening File Explorer
slides.content:
1. File Explorer: Organizes documents, photos, etc.
  2. Open: Click File Explorer icon or search “File Explorer.”
  3. Shows folders like “Documents,” “Downloads.”
    4. Activity: Open File Explorer and look at folders.

slides.title: Creating a Folder
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Open File Explorer.
  2. Step 2: Right-click → New → Folder.
  3. Step 3: Name it “My Files 2025.”
  4. Why? Keep letters, budgets organized.
    5. Activity: Create a folder named “My Files 2025.”

slides.title: Saving a File
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Open a document (e.g., text file).
  2. Step 2: Click File → Save As.
  3. Step 3: Choose “My Files 2025” folder; name file (e.g., “Notes”).
    4. Activity: Save a text file in your new folder.

slides.title: Using the Calculator App
slides.content:
1. Open: Search “Calculator” in taskbar.
  2. Use for budgets, expenses.
  3. Example: $100 budget ÷ 5 items = $20/item.
    4. Activity: Calculate a sample expense (e.g., $50 ÷ 4).

slides.title: Practical Activity
slides.content:
1. Task 1: Create a “My Files 2025” folder.
  2. Task 2: Save a text file (“Notes”) in the folder.
  3. Task 3: Calculate $60 ÷ 3 items.
    4. Activity: Complete each task and celebrate your progress!

slides.title: Why This Matters
slides.content:
1. Organize personal documents.
  2. Calculate expenses quickly.
  3. Prepare for typing next week!
    4. Activity: List one way these skills will help you in daily life.

slides.title: Q&A and Homework
slides.content:
1. Ask: Any questions about today?
  2. Homework:
    1. Turn on/off computer 3 times.
    2. Create a folder and save a file.
    3. Calculate a simple expense.
  3. Next Week: Typing and creating documents!
    4. Activity: Choose one homework task and do it before the next class.

slides.title: Typing and Document Creation
slides.content:
1. Objective: Learn to type and make documents.
  2. Today: Use Microsoft Word to write and save letters.
  3. Why It Matters: Create letters, lists, or notes easily!
  4. What kind of document would you like to write? (e.g., a letter to a friend)

slides.title: What Is Microsoft Word?
slides.content:
1. A program to type and format documents.
  2. Examples: Letters, to-do lists, invitations.
  3. Alternative: Google Docs (works in a browser).
⭐ Activity: Open Word or Google Docs on your computer.

slides.title: Opening Microsoft Word
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Click Start (Windows icon, bottom-left).
  2. Step 2: Type “Word” in the search bar.
  3. Step 3: Click Microsoft Word to open.
⭐ Activity: Open Word on your own computer.

slides.title: Understanding the Keyboard
slides.content:
1. Letters: Type words (e.g., A, B, C).
  2. Numbers: At the top or number pad.
  3. Spacebar: Add spaces between words.
  4. Enter: Start a new line.
  5. Backspace: Delete mistakes.
⭐ Activity: Touch the keys on a real keyboard.

slides.title: Typing Your First Words
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Open Word (blank document).
  2. Step 2: Click in the white area.
  3. Step 3: Type a sentence (e.g., “Hello, my name is [Your Name]”).
  4. Use Backspace to fix mistakes.
⭐ Activity: Type your name.

slides.title: Saving Your Document
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Click File → Save As.
  2. Step 2: Choose “My Files 2025” folder (from Week 1).
  3. Step 3: Name file (e.g., “My Letter”).
  4. Step 4: Click Save.
⭐ Activity: Save your document in the Module 1 folder.

slides.title: Formatting Text
slides.content:
1. Bold: Highlight text, click Bold (B icon).
  2. Font Size: Change size (e.g., 14pt for body, 16pt for titles).
  3. Alignment: Center text (e.g., for a title).
⭐ Activity: Use the formatting toolbar to change text style and color.

slides.title: Creating a Letter
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Type a title (e.g., “Dear Friend”).
  2. Step 2: Press Enter for a new line.
  3. Step 3: Type 2-3 sentences (e.g., “I hope you’re well. Let’s meet soon.”).
  4. Step 4: Format title (Bold, Center, 16pt).
✉️ Guide: Help learners type and format a short letter.

slides.title: Using Bullets for Lists
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Click the Bullets icon in Word.
  2. Step 2: Type items (e.g., “Buy groceries,” “Call friend”).
  3. Step 3: Press Enter to add more items.
📝 Activity: Learners create a to-do list.

slides.title: Saving and Closing
slides.content:
1. Save: Click File → Save (or Ctrl+S) to update.
  2. Close: Click File → Close or the red X (top-right).
  3. Reopen: Open File Explorer, find “My Files 2025,” double-click file.
⭐ Activity: Save and reopen your file.

slides.title: Practical Activity
slides.content:
1. Task 1: Open Word and type a short letter (3 sentences).
  2. Task 2: Format the title (Bold, Center, 16pt).
  3. Task 3: Save the letter as “My Letter” in “My Files 2025.”
  4. Task 4: Create a bulleted to-do list (3 items).
✅ Checklist: Complete each task and celebrate progress!

slides.title: Why This Matters
slides.content:
1. Write letters to friends or family.
  2. Create lists for planning or tasks.
  3. Prepare for spreadsheets next week!
⏳ Note: These skills help in daily life.

slides.title: Q&A and Homework
slides.content:
1. Ask: Any questions about typing or Word?
  2. Homework:
    1. Type a 3-sentence letter and save it.
    2. Create a bulleted list of 3 tasks.
    3. Reopen your saved letter.
  3. Next Week: Spreadsheets for organizing numbers!
❓ Encourage: Ask questions and use handouts for practice.

slides.title: Introduction to Spreadsheets
slides.content:
1. Objective: Learn to organize numbers and lists.
  2. Today: Use Excel to track expenses and calculate totals.
  3. Why It Matters: Manage budgets or plans easily!
  4. What would you like to track? (e.g., grocery expenses)

slides.title: What Is Microsoft Excel?
slides.content:
1. A program to organize numbers and lists in tables.
  2. Examples: Budgets, event plans, shopping lists.
  3. Alternative: Google Sheets (works in a browser).
⭐ Activity: Open Excel or Google Sheets on your computer.

slides.title: Opening Microsoft Excel
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Click Start (Windows icon, bottom-left).
  2. Step 2: Type “Excel” in the search bar.
  3. Step 3: Click Microsoft Excel to open.
⭐ Activity: Open Excel on your own computer.

slides.title: Understanding Spreadsheets
slides.content:
1. Cells: Boxes where you type data (e.g., A1, B2).
  2. Rows: Horizontal lines (numbered 1, 2, 3...).
  3. Columns: Vertical lines (lettered A, B, C...).
  4. Example: Type “Groceries” in cell A1.
⭐ Activity: Find and name cells, rows, and columns in a spreadsheet.

slides.title: Entering Data
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Click a cell (e.g., A1).
  2. Step 2: Type data (e.g., “Milk” or “$5”).
  3. Step 3: Press Enter to move to the next cell.
  4. Tip: Use arrow keys to move between cells.
⭐ Activity: Type a simple list in Excel.

slides.title: Saving Your Spreadsheet
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Click File → Save As.
  2. Step 2: Choose “My Files 2025” folder (from Week 1).
  3. Step 3: Name file (e.g., “My Budget”).
  4. Step 4: Click Save.
⭐ Activity: Save your spreadsheet in the Module 3 folder.

slides.title: Basic Formatting
slides.content:
1. Bold: Highlight cell, click Bold (B icon).
  2. Borders: Add lines around cells (Border icon).
  3. Column Width: Drag column edges to fit text.
⭐ Activity: Format and adjust columns in your spreadsheet.

slides.title: Simple Calculations (SUM)
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Type numbers (e.g., $5, $10, $15 in B1:B3).
  2. Step 2: Click a cell for the total (e.g., B4).
  3. Step 3: Type =SUM(B1:B3) and press Enter.
  4. Example: $5 + $10 + $15 = $30.
⭐ Activity: Calculate a total using the SUM formula.

slides.title: Creating an Expense Tracker
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Label A1: “Item,” B1: “Cost.”
  2. Step 2: Enter items (e.g., “Milk,” “Bread” in A2:A3).
  3. Step 3: Enter costs (e.g., $2, $3 in B2:B3).
  4. Step 4: Use SUM in B4 to calculate total.
📋 Guide: Help learners build a tracker.

slides.title: Checking Your Work
slides.content:
1. Check: Are numbers correct? Is text clear?
  2. Save: Click File → Save (or Ctrl+S).
  3. Reopen: Open File Explorer, find “My Files 2025,” double-click file.
⭐ Activity: Save and reopen your file.

slides.title: Practical Activity
slides.content:
1. Task 1: Open Excel and create an expense tracker.
  2. Task 2: Enter 3 items and costs (e.g., “Milk,” $2).
  3. Task 3: Use SUM to calculate total cost.
  4. Task 4: Save as “My Budget” in “My Files 2025.”
✅ Checklist: Complete each task and celebrate progress!

slides.title: Why This Matters
slides.content:
1. Track expenses (e.g., groceries, bills).
  2. Organize lists (e.g., events, tasks).
  3. Prepare for email next week!
⏳ Note: Spreadsheets help in real life.

slides.title: Q&A and Homework
slides.content:
1. Ask: Any questions about Excel?
  2. Homework:
    1. Create an expense tracker with 5 items.
    2. Calculate the total using SUM.
    3. Save and reopen the file.
  3. Next Week: Sending emails!
❓ Encourage: Ask questions and use handouts for practice.

slides.title: Email Setup and Communication
slides.content:
1. Objective: Learn to use email for communication.
  2. Today: Set up Gmail and send messages.
  3. Why It Matters: Stay in touch with friends or family!
  4. Who would you like to email? (e.g., a family member)

slides.title: What Is Email?
slides.content:
1. A way to send and receive messages online.
  2. Examples: Send a thank-you note, share a document.
  3. We’ll use Gmail, a free email service.
📧 Explain: Email is like a digital letter; show Gmail on a projector.

slides.title: Opening Gmail
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Open Google Chrome (browser).
  2. Step 2: Type “gmail.com” in the address bar.
  3. Step 3: Press Enter to go to Gmail.
⭐ Activity: Open Gmail on your own computer.

slides.title: Creating a Gmail Account
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Click “Create account” on Gmail.
  2. Step 2: Enter your name, birthday, and password.
  3. Step 3: Choose an email address (e.g., yourname@gmail.com).
  4. Step 4: Sign in with your email and password.
📝 Help: Assist learners to create accounts; write down passwords securely.

slides.title: Understanding the Gmail Inbox
slides.content:
1. Inbox: Shows received emails.
  2. Compose: Button to write a new email.
  3. Sent: Shows emails you’ve sent.
⭐ Activity: Find and name the key areas in your Gmail inbox.

slides.title: Writing an Email
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Click “Compose” in Gmail.
  2. Step 2: Type recipient’s email in “To” field.
  3. Step 3: Add a subject (e.g., “Hello”).
  4. Step 4: Type a message (e.g., “Hi, hope you’re well!”).
  5. Step 5: Click “Send.”
⭐ Activity: Send an email to a classmate.

slides.title: Attaching a File
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Click “Compose” and write an email.
  2. Step 2: Click the paperclip icon (“Attach files”).
  3. Step 3: Choose a file from “My Files 2025” (e.g., “My Letter”).
  4. Step 4: Click “Send.”
⭐ Activity: Attach a document to an email.

slides.title: Replying to an Email
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Open an email in your inbox.
  2. Step 2: Click “Reply” at the bottom.
  3. Step 3: Type your response (e.g., “Thanks for your message!”).
  4. Step 4: Click “Send.”
⭐ Activity: Reply to an email you receive.

slides.title: Organizing Your Inbox
slides.content:
1. Delete: Remove unwanted emails (click trash icon).
  2. Archive: Hide emails without deleting (click archive icon).
  3. Folders/Labels: Group emails (e.g., “Family” or “Work”).
⭐ Activity: Delete an email from your inbox.

slides.title: Checking Your Work
slides.content:
1. Check: Did your email send? Check “Sent” folder.
  2. Sign Out: Click your profile picture → “Sign out.”
  3. Sign In: Reopen Gmail, enter email and password.
⭐ Activity: Sign in and out of Gmail.

slides.title: Practical Activity
slides.content:
1. Task 1: Create a Gmail account (or sign in).
  2. Task 2: Send an email with a subject and 2 sentences.
  3. Task 3: Attach a file (e.g., “My Letter” from Week 2).
  4. Task 4: Reply to an email from the instructor.
✅ Checklist: Complete each task and celebrate progress!

slides.title: Why This Matters
slides.content:
1. Send messages to friends or family.
  2. Share documents (e.g., letters, lists).
  3. Prepare for internet safety next week!
⏳ Note: Email is useful in daily life.

slides.title: Q&A and Homework
slides.content:
1. Ask: Any questions about Gmail?
  2. Homework:
    1. Send an email to a friend or family member.
    2. Attach a file to an email.
    3. Reply to an email or check your inbox.
  3. Next Week: Using the internet safely!
❓ Encourage: Ask questions and use handouts for practice.

slides.title: Internet and Online Safety
slides.content:
1. Objective: Learn to use the internet and stay safe.
  2. Today: Browse with Google Chrome and avoid scams.
  3. Why It Matters: Find information and protect yourself!
  4. What do you want to find online? (e.g., a recipe)

slides.title: What Is the Internet?
slides.content:
1. A global network to find information and connect.
  2. Examples: Search for news, recipes, or weather.
  3. We’ll use Google Chrome, a web browser.
🌐 Explain: The internet is a digital library; show Chrome.

slides.title: Opening Google Chrome
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Click Start (Windows icon, bottom-left).
  2. Step 2: Type “Chrome” in the search bar.
  3. Step 3: Click Google Chrome to open.
⭐ Activity: Open Chrome on your own computer.

slides.title: Understanding a Web Browser
slides.content:
1. Address Bar: Type website names (e.g., www.google.com).
  2. Tabs: Open multiple websites at once.
  3. Back/Forward Buttons: Navigate between pages.
⭐ Activity: Find and name the address bar and tabs in your browser.

slides.title: Searching the Internet
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Open Chrome and go to www.google.com.
  2. Step 2: Type a question (e.g., “easy dinner recipes”).
  3. Step 3: Press Enter to see results.
  4. Step 4: Click a link to visit a website.
⭐ Activity: Search for a topic of interest online.

slides.title: Saving Favorite Websites
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Visit a website (e.g., www.bbc.com).
  2. Step 2: Click the star icon in the address bar.
  3. Step 3: Name the bookmark (e.g., “News”).
  4. Step 4: Click Bookmarks menu to reopen.
⭐ Activity: Bookmark a favorite site.

slides.title: Staying Safe Online
slides.content:
1. HTTPS: Look for “https://” in website addresses (secure).
  2. Avoid Suspicious Links: Don’t click unknown links.
  3. Strong Passwords: Use letters, numbers, symbols (e.g., Sunny2025!).
🔒 Discuss: Safe vs. unsafe websites.

slides.title: Recognizing Phishing Emails
slides.content:
1. Phishing: Fake emails asking for personal info.
  2. Red Flags:
    1. Unknown sender (e.g., random123@email.com).
    2. Urgent demands (e.g., “Send money now!”).
    3. Strange links or attachments.
  3. Action: Delete or report as spam.
⭐ Activity: Look at an example of a fake email and discuss why it is dangerous.

slides.title: Safe Browsing Habits
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Check for “https://” before entering info.
  2. Step 2: Don’t share personal details (e.g., bank info).
  3. Step 3: Log out of websites (e.g., Gmail) when done.
⭐ Activity: Sign out of Gmail.

slides.title: Practical Activity
slides.content:
1. Task 1: Open Chrome and search for “weather forecast.”
  2. Task 2: Bookmark a favorite website (e.g., a news site).
  3. Task 3: Review a sample email and identify if it’s phishing.
  4. Task 4: Sign out of Gmail and sign back in.
✅ Checklist: Complete each task and celebrate progress!

slides.title: Why This Matters
slides.content:
1. Find recipes, news, or tips online.
  2. Stay safe from scams and phishing.
  3. Prepare for advanced spreadsheets next week!
⏳ Note: Internet skills help in real life.

slides.title: Q&A and Homework
slides.content:
1. Ask: Any questions about browsing or safety?
  2. Homework:
    1. Search for a topic (e.g., “gardening tips”).
    2. Bookmark a website you like.
    3. Check your Gmail for suspicious emails.
  3. Next Week: Advanced spreadsheets!
❓ Encourage: Ask questions and use handouts for practice.

slides.title: Advanced Spreadsheets
slides.content:
1. Objective: Learn advanced spreadsheet skills.
  2. Today: Use formulas and charts in Excel.
  3. Why It Matters: Analyze budgets or plans easily!
  4. What numbers do you want to analyze? (e.g., monthly expenses)

slides.title: Why Advanced Spreadsheets?
slides.content:
1. Use formulas to calculate automatically.
  2. Create charts to visualize data.
  3. Examples: Track payments, show spending trends.
📊 Recap: Review Week 3 basics (cells, SUM); show Excel.

slides.title: Reviewing Excel Basics
slides.content:
1. Cells: Boxes for data (e.g., A1).
  2. Rows/Columns: Horizontal/vertical lines.
  3. SUM: Adds numbers (e.g., =SUM(B1:B3)).
  4. Open Excel: Start → Type “Excel” → Click.
⭐ Activity: Open Excel and review your tracker file.

slides.title: Using the IF Formula
slides.content:
1. IF Formula: Checks conditions (e.g., “Is budget over $100?”).
  2. Step 1: Type expenses in B1:B3 (e.g., $50, $120, $80).
  3. Step 2: In C1, type =IF(B1>100,"High","Low").
  4. Step 3: Press Enter; copy to C2:C3.
⭐ Activity: Use the IF formula to label expenses as “High” or “Low.”

slides.title: Using VLOOKUP
slides.content:
1. VLOOKUP: Finds data in a table (e.g., item prices).
  2. Step 1: Create a price list (e.g., A1:A2 = “Milk,” “Bread”; B1:B2 = $2, $3).
  3. Step 2: In D1, type =VLOOKUP("Milk",A1:B2,2,FALSE).
  4. Step 3: Press Enter (shows $2).
⭐ Activity: Use VLOOKUP to find specific data in your spreadsheet.

slides.title: Creating a Chart
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Enter data (e.g., months in A1:A3, expenses in B1:B3).
  2. Step 2: Highlight data (A1:B3).
  3. Step 3: Click Insert → Column Chart.
  4. Step 4: Add title (e.g., “Monthly Expenses”).
⭐ Activity: Create a chart in Excel.

slides.title: Sorting Data
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Enter items and prices (e.g., A1:A3, B1:B3).
  2. Step 2: Highlight data (A1:B3).
  3. Step 3: Click Data → Sort → Sort by Price (High to Low).
⭐ Activity: Sort a list in Excel.

slides.title: Filtering Data
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Add headers (e.g., “Item,” “Price”).
  2. Step 2: Click Data → Filter.
  3. Step 3: Click dropdown in Price; select “Greater than $10.”
⭐ Activity: Use filters to hide irrelevant data in your spreadsheet.

slides.title: Creating a Payment Schedule
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Label A1:B1 as “Month,” “Payment.”
  2. Step 2: Enter months (e.g., Jan, Feb in A2:A4).
  3. Step 3: Enter payments (e.g., $50, $60, $70 in B2:B4).
  4. Step 4: Use SUM in B5; create a chart.
📅 Guide: Build a payment schedule together.

slides.title: Saving and Reviewing
slides.content:
1. Save: Click File → Save As → “My Files 2025” → “My Schedule.”
  2. Check: Review formulas and chart for errors.
  3. Reopen: Open File Explorer, double-click file.
⭐ Activity: Save and reopen your file.

slides.title: Practical Activity
slides.content:
1. Task 1: Create a payment schedule (3 months, payments).
  2. Task 2: Use SUM to calculate total.
  3. Task 3: Create a column chart.
  4. Task 4: Save as “My Schedule” in “My Files 2025.”
✅ Checklist: Complete each task and celebrate progress!

slides.title: Why This Matters
slides.content:
1. Analyze budgets or schedules.
  2. Visualize data with charts.
  3. Prepare for presentations next week!
⏳ Note: Advanced spreadsheets help in real life.

slides.title: Q&A and Homework
slides.content:
1. Ask: Any questions about Excel?
  2. Homework:
    1. Create a payment schedule with 4 entries.
    2. Add a SUM formula and a chart.
    3. Save and reopen the file.
  3. Next Week: Creating presentations!
❓ Encourage: Ask questions and use handouts for practice.

slides.title: Creating Presentations
slides.content:
1. Objective: Learn to make and share slide presentations.
  2. Today: Use PowerPoint to create slides.
  3. Why It Matters: Share ideas clearly (e.g., plans, hobbies)!
  4. What would you like to present? (e.g., a trip plan)

slides.title: What Is Microsoft PowerPoint?
slides.content:
1. A program to create slides for presentations.
  2. Examples: Share a travel plan, show a budget.
  3. Alternative: Google Slides (works in a browser).
⭐ Activity: Open PowerPoint or Google Slides on your computer.

slides.title: Opening Microsoft PowerPoint
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Click Start (Windows icon, bottom-left).
  2. Step 2: Type “PowerPoint” in the search bar.
  3. Step 3: Click Microsoft PowerPoint to open.
⭐ Activity: Open PowerPoint on your own computer.

slides.title: Understanding PowerPoint
slides.content:
1. Slides: Pages in your presentation.
  2. Slide Pane: Left side shows all slides.
  3. Toolbar: Top has tools (e.g., text, images).
⭐ Activity: Find and name the slide pane and toolbar in PowerPoint.

slides.title: Creating a New Slide
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Open PowerPoint (blank presentation).
  2. Step 2: Click Home → New Slide.
  3. Step 3: Choose a layout (e.g., Title and Content).
⭐ Activity: Add a slide to your presentation.

slides.title: Adding Text to a Slide
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Click in the title box; type (e.g., “My Travel Plan”).
  2. Step 2: Click in the content box; type (e.g., “Visit Paris”).
  3. Step 3: Format text (e.g., Bold, 20pt font).
⭐ Activity: Type a title and text on a slide.

slides.title: Inserting an Image
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Click Insert → Pictures.
  2. Step 2: Choose an image from “My Files 2025” (e.g., a photo).
  3. Step 3: Resize by dragging corners.
⭐ Activity: Insert and resize an image in your slide.

slides.title: Using Templates
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Click Design → Themes.
  2. Step 2: Choose a theme (e.g., colorful background).
  3. Step 3: Apply to all slides for consistency.
⭐ Activity: Apply a theme to your presentation.

slides.title: Creating a 3-Slide Presentation
slides.content:
1. Slide 1: Title (e.g., “My Summer Plan”).
  2. Slide 2: List 3 items (e.g., places to visit).
  3. Slide 3: Add an image and a sentence.
🗂️ Guide: Build a short presentation together.

slides.title: Saving and Presenting
slides.content:
1. Save: Click File → Save As → “My Files 2025” → “My Presentation.”
  2. Present: Click Slide Show → From Beginning.
  3. Navigate: Click or press arrow keys to move slides.
⭐ Activity: Save and present your slides.

slides.title: Practical Activity
slides.content:
1. Task 1: Create a 3-slide presentation.
  2. Task 2: Add a title, text, and an image.
  3. Task 3: Apply a theme.
  4. Task 4: Save as “My Presentation” and present it.
✅ Checklist: Complete each task and celebrate progress!

slides.title: Why This Matters
slides.content:
1. Share ideas (e.g., travel plans, hobbies).
  2. Present information clearly.
  3. Prepare for virtual meetings next week!
⏳ Note: Presentations help in real life.

slides.title: Q&A and Homework
slides.content:
1. Ask: Any questions about PowerPoint?
  2. Homework:
    1. Create a 3-slide presentation about a hobby.
    2. Add text, an image, and a theme.
    3. Save and practice presenting.
  3. Next Week: Virtual meetings with Zoom!
❓ Encourage: Ask questions and use handouts for practice.

slides.title: Virtual Meetings
slides.content:
1. Objective: Learn to use Zoom for online meetings.
  2. Today: Join, manage, and share in Zoom meetings.
  3. Why It Matters: Connect with friends or groups remotely!
  4. Who would you like to meet online? (e.g., family)

slides.title: What Is Zoom?
slides.content:
1. A program for video calls and meetings.
  2. Examples: Chat with family, discuss plans.
  3. Free to use for basic features.
🖥️ Show: Display Zoom on a projector; explain as a video phone.

slides.title: Opening Zoom
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Click Start (Windows icon, bottom-left).
  2. Step 2: Type “Zoom” in the search bar.
  3. Step 3: Click Zoom to open.
  4. Alternative: Open Chrome, go to zoom.us, click “Join a Meeting.”
🖱️ Demo: Show how to open Zoom; help learners as needed.

slides.title: Joining a Zoom Meeting
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Get a meeting ID (e.g., from an email).
  2. Step 2: Open Zoom, click “Join.”
  3. Step 3: Enter meeting ID and your name.
  4. Step 4: Click “Join Meeting.”
🔗 Practice: Join a test meeting with a sample ID.

slides.title: Using Zoom Controls
slides.content:
1. Mute/Unmute: Turn microphone off/on.
  2. Video On/Off: Show/hide your camera.
  3. Participants: See who’s in the meeting.
  4. Leave: Click to exit the meeting.
🎛️ Show: Controls in a real Zoom meeting.

slides.title: Sharing Your Screen
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Join a Zoom meeting.
  2. Step 2: Click “Share Screen.”
  3. Step 3: Choose a window (e.g., PowerPoint from Week 7).
  4. Step 4: Click “Share.”
🖥️ Practice: Share a Week 7 presentation.

slides.title: Scheduling a Meeting
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Open Zoom, click “Schedule.”
  2. Step 2: Set date, time, and topic (e.g., “Family Chat”).
  3. Step 3: Copy meeting ID and link.
  4. Step 4: Email the link (use Gmail from Week 4).
📅 Show: Schedule a meeting and copy the link.

slides.title: Testing Your Audio and Video
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Join a test meeting (e.g., zoom.us/test).
  2. Step 2: Test microphone (speak, check sound bars).
  3. Step 3: Test video (turn on camera, check image).
🎤 Practice: Run a test meeting in class.

slides.title: Etiquette for Zoom Meetings
slides.content:
1. Mute: Turn off microphone when not speaking.
  2. Background: Choose a tidy or virtual background.
  3. Focus: Avoid distractions during meetings.
🤝 Discuss: Polite Zoom behavior.

slides.title: Practical Activity
slides.content:
1. Task 1: Join a test Zoom meeting.
  2. Task 2: Practice mute/unmute and video on/off.
  3. Task 3: Share a PowerPoint slide from Week 7.
  4. Task 4: Schedule a meeting and copy the link.
✅ Checklist: Complete each task and celebrate progress!

slides.title: Why This Matters
slides.content:
1. Connect with friends or family online.
  2. Share ideas in meetings.
  3. Prepare for cloud storage next week!
⏳ Note: Virtual meetings help in real life.

slides.title: Q&A and Homework
slides.content:
1. Ask: Any questions about Zoom?
  2. Homework:
    1. Join a test Zoom meeting (use zoom.us/test).
    2. Share a file or slide in a meeting.
    3. Schedule a meeting and email the link.
  3. Next Week: Cloud storage with Google Drive!
❓ Encourage: Ask questions and use handouts for practice.

slides.title: Cloud Storage and Collaboration
slides.content:
1. Objective: Learn to save and share files online.
  2. Today: Use Google Drive to store and collaborate.
  3. Why It Matters: Access files anywhere, share safely!
  4. What files would you like to store? (e.g., photos)

slides.title: What Is Google Drive?
slides.content:
1. A free online storage service for files.
  2. Examples: Save photos, documents, or presentations.
  3. Access from any computer or phone with internet.
🗄️ Explain: Drive is a digital filing cabinet; show Drive.

slides.title: Accessing Google Drive
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Open Google Chrome.
  2. Step 2: Go to drive.google.com.
  3. Step 3: Sign in with your Gmail account (from Week 4).
🌐 Demo: Show how to open Drive; help learners as needed.

slides.title: Understanding Google Drive
slides.content:
1. My Drive: Where your files are stored.
  2. New Button: Add files or folders.
  3. Shared with Me: Files others share with you.
📁 Show: Point to key areas in a real Drive interface.

slides.title: Uploading a File
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Click “New” → “File upload.”
  2. Step 2: Choose a file from “My Files 2025” (e.g., “My Presentation”).
  3. Step 3: Click “Open” to upload.
⬆️ Practice: Upload a Week 7 presentation.

slides.title: Creating a Folder
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Click “New” → “Folder.”
  2. Step 2: Name it (e.g., “Photos 2025”).
  3. Step 3: Upload files into the folder.
🗂️ Practice: Create a folder and organize files.

slides.title: Sharing a File
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Right-click a file (e.g., “My Presentation”).
  2. Step 2: Click “Share” → Add email address.
  3. Step 3: Choose “View only” or “Can edit.”
  4. Step 4: Click “Send” to share via Gmail.
🔗 Practice: Share a file with view-only access.

slides.title: Collaborating on a File
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Share a file with “Can edit” access.
  2. Step 2: Open file (e.g., Google Docs in Drive).
  3. Step 3: Edit together in real-time.
👥 Demo: Real-time editing with a test file.

slides.title: Downloading a File
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Right-click a file in Google Drive.
  2. Step 2: Click “Download.”
  3. Step 3: Save to “My Files 2025” folder.
⬇️ Practice: Download a file from Drive.

slides.title: Practical Activity
slides.content:
1. Task 1: Upload a file to Google Drive (e.g., “My Presentation”).
  2. Task 2: Create a folder “Photos 2025” and move a file into it.
  3. Task 3: Share a file with view-only access.
  4. Task 4: Download a file to “My Files 2025.”
✅ Checklist: Complete each task and celebrate progress!

slides.title: Why This Matters
slides.content:
1. Store photos, documents safely.
  2. Share files with friends or family.
  3. Prepare for PDFs next week!
⏳ Note: Cloud storage helps in real life.

slides.title: Q&A and Homework
slides.content:
1. Ask: Any questions about Google Drive?
  2. Homework:
    1. Upload 2 files to Google Drive.
    2. Create a folder and move a file into it.
    3. Share a file with someone via email.
  3. Next Week: Working with PDFs!
❓ Encourage: Ask questions and use handouts for practice.

slides.title: Working with PDFs
slides.content:
1. Objective: Learn to view and annotate PDFs.
  2. Today: Use Adobe Acrobat Reader to manage documents.
  3. Why It Matters: Read and mark up files like forms or recipes!
  4. What PDFs have you seen? (e.g., a bill or form)

slides.title: What Is a PDF?
slides.content:
1. A file format for documents that look the same everywhere.
  2. Examples: Recipes, forms, manuals.
  3. Use Adobe Acrobat Reader (free) to open and edit.
📄 Explain: PDFs are “fixed” documents; show Acrobat Reader.

slides.title: Opening Adobe Acrobat Reader
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Click Start (Windows icon, bottom-left).
  2. Step 2: Type “Adobe Acrobat” in the search bar.
  3. Step 3: Click Adobe Acrobat Reader to open.
🖱️ Demo: Show how to open Acrobat; ensure it’s installed.

slides.title: Opening a PDF
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Open File Explorer, go to “My Files 2025.”
  2. Step 2: Double-click a PDF file (e.g., “Recipe.pdf”).
  3. Alternative: In Acrobat, click File → Open, select file.
📂 Practice: Open a sample PDF for practice.

slides.title: Navigating a PDF
slides.content:
1. Scroll: Use mouse wheel or sidebar to move up/down.
  2. Zoom: Click View → Zoom In/Out.
  3. Page Navigation: Use arrows to change pages.
🧭 Show: Navigation in a multi-page PDF.

slides.title: Highlighting Text
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Open a PDF in Acrobat Reader.
  2. Step 2: Click the Highlight tool (marker icon).
  3. Step 3: Drag over text to highlight (e.g., a recipe step).
🖍️ Practice: Highlight a sample PDF.

slides.title: Adding Comments
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Click the Comment tool (speech bubble icon).
  2. Step 2: Click where you want to add a note.
  3. Step 3: Type your comment (e.g., “Try this recipe!”).
💬 Demo: Add a comment to a PDF.

slides.title: Saving an Edited PDF
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Click File → Save As.
  2. Step 2: Choose “My Files 2025” folder.
  3. Step 3: Name file (e.g., “Recipe_Edited.pdf”).
💾 Practice: Save an edited PDF.

slides.title: Emailing a PDF
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Open Gmail (from Week 4).
  2. Step 2: Click Compose, attach PDF from “My Files 2025.”
  3. Step 3: Add recipient and subject, click Send.
📧 Practice: Email a PDF file.

slides.title: Practical Activity
slides.content:
1. Task 1: Open a sample PDF in Acrobat Reader.
  2. Task 2: Highlight a sentence and add a comment.
  3. Task 3: Save as “Edited_PDF” in “My Files 2025.”
  4. Task 4: Email the PDF to the instructor.
✅ Checklist: Complete each task and celebrate progress!

slides.title: Why This Matters
slides.content:
1. View forms, recipes, or manuals.
  2. Add notes to important documents.
  3. Prepare for combining documents next week!
⏳ Note: PDF skills help in real life.

slides.title: Q&A and Homework
slides.content:
1. Ask: Any questions about PDFs?
  2. Homework:
    1. Open and highlight a PDF.
    2. Add a comment and save the file.
    3. Email the edited PDF to a friend.
  3. Next Week: Combining documents and spreadsheets!
❓ Encourage: Ask questions and use handouts for practice.

slides.title: Document and Spreadsheet Integration
slides.content:
1. Objective: Create reports with text and data.
  2. Today: Use Word, Excel, and Google Drive together.
  3. Why It Matters: Make clear reports (e.g., budgets, plans)!
  4. What kind of report would you make? (e.g., a budget)

slides.title: Why Combine Tools?
slides.content:
1. Word: Write professional reports or letters.
  2. Excel: Organize and visualize data (e.g., charts).
  3. Google Drive: Store and share your work.
🗂️ Recap: Week 2 (Word), Week 6 (Excel), Week 9 (Drive).

slides.title: Reviewing Word and Excel
slides.content:
1. Word: Type and format text (Week 2).
  2. Excel: Use formulas and charts (Weeks 3, 6).
  3. Open: Start → Type “Word” or “Excel” → Click.
🖱️ Demo: Open both programs and review basics.

slides.title: Creating a Data Table in Excel
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Open Excel, label A1:B1 as “Item,” “Cost.”
  2. Step 2: Enter data (e.g., “Food,” $50; “Travel,” $30).
  3. Step 3: Use SUM for total (e.g., B3: =SUM(B1:B2)).
📊 Practice: Create a table in Excel.

slides.title: Creating a Chart in Excel
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Highlight table (e.g., A1:B2).
  2. Step 2: Click Insert → Column Chart.
  3. Step 3: Add title (e.g., “Monthly Budget”).
📈 Practice: Create a chart in Excel.

slides.title: Copying a Chart to Word
slides.content:
1. Step 1: In Excel, right-click chart → Copy.
  2. Step 2: Open Word, click where you want the chart.
  3. Step 3: Press Ctrl+V to paste.
📋 Demo: Copy and paste a chart into Word.

slides.title: Writing a Report in Word
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Open Word, type a title (e.g., “Budget Report”).
  2. Step 2: Add text (e.g., “This shows my expenses.”).
  3. Step 3: Paste Excel chart below text.
  4. Step 4: Format (Bold title, 16pt).
📝 Guide: Write a short report in Word.

slides.title: Saving Your Report
slides.content:
1. Step 1: In Word, click File → Save As.
  2. Step 2: Choose “My Files 2025” folder.
  3. Step 3: Name file (e.g., “My Report”).
💾 Practice: Save your report in Word.

slides.title: Uploading to Google Drive
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Open Google Drive (drive.google.com).
  2. Step 2: Click “New” → “File upload.”
  3. Step 3: Select “My Report” from “My Files 2025.”
  4. Step 4: Share with view-only access (Week 9).
🌐 Practice: Upload and share your report.

slides.title: Practical Activity
slides.content:
1. Task 1: Create an Excel table with 3 items and costs.
  2. Task 2: Add a SUM formula and a column chart.
  3. Task 3: Create a Word report with text and pasted chart.
  4. Task 4: Save and upload to Google Drive.
✅ Checklist: Complete each task and celebrate progress!

slides.title: Why This Matters
slides.content:
1. Create clear reports with data.
  2. Share plans or budgets easily.
  3. Prepare for the capstone project next week!
⏳ Note: Integration skills help in real life.

slides.title: Q&A and Homework
slides.content:
1. Ask: Any questions about Word, Excel, or Drive?
  2. Homework:
    1. Create a report with an Excel chart.
    2. Save and upload to Google Drive.
    3. Share with a friend via email.
  3. Next Week: Capstone project!
❓ Encourage: Ask questions and use handouts for practice.

slides.title: Artificial Intelligence – Your New Digital Assistant
slides.content:
1. Learn how AI can save you time, help you make better decisions, and open new opportunities.
💡 Reflection: Have you ever heard of AI before? What do you think it does?
Write down your thoughts or say them aloud.

slides.title: What is AI?
slides.content:
1. AI means machines that can learn and make decisions.
  2. It uses data to find patterns and give smart answers.
  3. It’s not magic — it’s math + logic + examples.
🔍 Analogy: AI is like a smart student who learns from past papers and helps you solve new questions.

slides.title: Why Should You Care?
slides.content:
1. AI helps you do tasks faster.
  2. It gives better results than guessing.
  3. It can help you earn more or save more.
🤔 Think: What’s one task you do often that takes time? Imagine AI doing it for you.

slides.title: AI You Already Use Daily
slides.content:
1. M-Pesa: fraud alerts, transaction summaries.
  2. YouTube/TikTok: video suggestions.
  3. Google Translate: instant language help.
  4. Facebook: friend suggestions, auto-tagging photos.
📱 Quick Poll: Have you used any of these today? Think about which ones you use most often.

slides.title: AI for Small Business
slides.content:
1. Track sales trends automatically.
  2. Predict which products will sell more.
  3. Manage stock levels.
  4. Send targeted messages to customers.
🏪 Local Example: Imagine your shop knows which items will run out next week — that’s AI helping.

slides.title: AI for Personal Productivity
slides.content:
1. Voice-to-text: speak instead of typing.
  2. Smart typing: auto-complete messages.
  3. Calendar suggestions: best time to meet.
  4. Photo sorting: group by faces or places.
🎤 Try It: Use voice-to-text on your phone. Do you ever struggle with typing long messages?

slides.title: AI for Learning
slides.content:
1. Chatbots that explain topics in simple words.
  2. AI quizzes that adjust to your level.
  3. Apps that correct your pronunciation.
  4. Study summaries from long notes.
🧑‍💻 Demo: Ask ChatGPT or Bing Copilot a basic question. See how it answers!

slides.title: AI for Data Analysis
slides.content:
1. Automatically creates charts from data.
  2. Spots patterns you might miss.
  3. Writes summaries and recommendations.
  4. Saves hours of manual work.
📊 Showcase: See a sample Excel sheet, then an AI-generated chart and insight.

slides.title: Free AI Tools You Can Try Today
slides.content:
1. ChatGPT / Bing Copilot: Ask questions, get answers.
  2. Canva Magic Design: Create posters and graphics.
  3. Google Lens: Identify objects, translate signs.
  4. Grammarly: Improve your writing.
🌐 Explore: Try one of these tools after class and share your experience next time!

slides.title: How to Start Using AI
slides.content:
1. Pick one task you do often.
  2. Search for an AI tool that helps with it.
  3. Try it with small, safe data.
  4. Keep what works, drop what doesn’t.
📝 Example: Typing long messages? Use voice-to-text. Making posters? Try Canva.

slides.title: Skills to Work Well with AI
slides.content:
1. Ask clear questions (called prompts).
  2. Check AI’s answers — don’t trust blindly.
  3. Combine AI help with your own thinking.
💬 Prompt Practice: Good: “Give me 3 tips to grow a small shop in Kenya.” Bad: “Tell me about business.”

slides.title: Risks & How to Stay Safe
slides.content:
1. Don’t share private info (ID, passwords).
  2. Double-check facts — AI can be wrong.
  3. Don’t copy blindly — learn and improve.
  4. Keep learning — AI changes fast.
⚠️ Remember: AI is a helper, not a master. You’re still in control.

slides.title: Call to Action
slides.content:
1. Try one AI tool this week.
  2. Use it for one task (typing, learning, designing).
  3. Share your experience in the next class.
✅ Homework: Pick one tool, use it, and tell us what happened!

slides.title: Bonus: AI in Kenya
slides.content:
1. Local banks use AI for fraud detection.
  2. Kenyan startups use AI for agriculture (predicting weather, crop diseases).
  3. AI chatbots help with customer service in local businesses.
🌍 Discussion: Where else could AI help in our country?

slides.title: Bonus: The Future of AI
slides.content:
1. AI is getting better at understanding language and images.
  2. More jobs will use AI tools in the future.
  3. Learning AI basics now gives you an advantage.
🚀 Encouragement: You don’t need to be a programmer to use AI. Curiosity and practice are enough!

slides.title: Capstone Project and Review
slides.content:
1. Objective: Combine all skills for a final project.
  2. Today: Create, present, and share a report.
  3. Why It Matters: Use all tools in real life!
  4. What project would you like to create? (e.g., a budget)

slides.title: What Is the Capstone Project?
slides.content:
1. Create a budget report (Word, Excel).
  2. Present it (PowerPoint, Zoom).
  3. Share it (Google Drive, Gmail, PDF).
  4. Use all tools from Weeks 1-11.
🛠️ Explain: The project is a real-world task.

slides.title: Step 1 – Create an Excel Table
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Open Excel (Week 3, 6).
  2. Step 2: Label A1:B1 as “Item,” “Cost” (e.g., “Rent,” $500).
  3. Step 3: Enter 4 items; use SUM for total.
  4. Step 4: Create a column chart (Week 6).
📊 Practice: Create a budget table in Excel.

slides.title: Step 2 – Write a Report in Word
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Open Word (Week 2).
  2. Step 2: Type title (e.g., “My Budget Report”).
  3. Step 3: Add text (e.g., “This shows my expenses.”).
  4. Step 4: Copy-paste Excel chart (Week 11).
📝 Guide: Write a report in Word.

slides.title: Step 3 – Save as PDF
slides.content:
1. Step 1: In Word, click File → Save As.
  2. Step 2: Choose “PDF” format, save in “My Files 2025.”
  3. Step 3: Open in Acrobat Reader to check (Week 10).
📄 Practice: Save as PDF and check in Acrobat.

slides.title: Step 4 – Create a Presentation
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Open PowerPoint (Week 7).
  2. Step 2: Create 3 slides (title, text, chart).
  3. Step 3: Apply a theme; add an image.
  4. Step 4: Save as “My Project” in “My Files 2025.”
📽️ Practice: Create slides for your project.

slides.title: Step 5 – Upload to Google Drive
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Open Google Drive (Week 9).
  2. Step 2: Upload Word, PDF, and PowerPoint files.
  3. Step 3: Create a folder “My Project 2025.”
☁️ Practice: Upload files to Drive.

slides.title: Step 6 – Share via Email
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Open Gmail (Week 4).
  2. Step 2: Compose email, attach PDF.
  3. Step 3: Share Google Drive link (view-only).
📧 Practice: Email your project files.

slides.title: Step 7 – Present in Zoom
slides.content:
1. Step 1: Join a Zoom meeting (Week 8).
  2. Step 2: Share PowerPoint via Screen Share.
  3. Step 3: Present slides, explain report.
🎤 Practice: Present your project in Zoom.

slides.title: Practical Activity
slides.content:
1. Task 1: Create Excel table and chart (4 items).
  2. Task 2: Write Word report with chart; save as PDF.
  3. Task 3: Create 3-slide PowerPoint.
  4. Task 4: Upload to Google Drive, share via Gmail, present in Zoom.
✅ Checklist: Complete each task and celebrate progress!

slides.title: Review of Skills
slides.content:
1. Week 1-2: Files, typing.
  2. Week 3-6: Spreadsheets, internet.
  3. Week 7-11: Presentations, Zoom, Drive, PDFs.
  4. Today: Combine all for real-world tasks!
🎉 Celebrate: Review all skills learned.

slides.title: Why This Matters
slides.content:
1. Create reports, budgets, or plans.
  2. Share and present ideas confidently.
  3. Use computers for daily life!
⏳ Note: Capstone skills help in real life.
